The Trump administration will abide by a court ruling to pause its creation of a nearly $1.8 billion fund meant to compensate people who say they were wrongly targeted by the government in the past, the Justice Department said in a statement Monday.

Meanwhile, Senate Majority Leader John Thune on Monday signaled that President Donald Trump needs to drop his push for a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund that has infuriated fellow Republicans and stalled the broader GOP agenda.

description:
Iran has suspended talks with the United States in protest over Israel’s actions in Lebanon, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported Monday.

Iran calls for the immediate halt of Israel’s wars in Gaza and Lebanon, along with the Israeli army’s full withdrawal from Lebanon, Tasnim said, adding that “until Iran’s and the resistance’s position on these matters is satisfied, there will be no negotiations.”

7:30 What Israel wants to achieve in Lebanon
8:59 Economics expert Iman Nasseri on what this means for oil prices

author: CNN
description:
The US carried out what it said was “self-defense” strikes in Iran over the weekend – as President Donald Trump sent back changes to a proposed deal to extend the existing ceasefire in the region and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. 

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed to have struck a US air base used to launch an attack on a telecommunications tower on Iran’s Sirik Island, according to a statement carried by several Iranian state-run news outlets. 

CNN international diplomatic editor Nic Robertson breaks down a statement from Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghlaibaf. Also, CNN global affairs analyst Kim Dozier and CNN military analyst Cedric Leighton react to the latest strikes, while CNN’s Ben Hunte discusses the latest developments with Middle East analyst Sina Azodi. 

Watch more CNN here: https://cnn.it/4kh5RPe

#Iran #Trump #News
title: Iran claims to strike US base; Trump changes deal proposal

author: CNN
description: 'Sue Tilley, the 60-something retired benefits supervisor and subject of British artist Lucian Freud's monumental painting "Sleeping by the Lion Carpet" (1996), has traveled from her home on the south coast of England to see the work before it heads to auction next month. The portrait is estimated to fetch between £25-35 million ($33-45M) at the Lewis Collection sale on June 24. But how does it feel to have your body up for auction for tens millions of dollars? We asked her.
title: The Face Behind a $45 Million Masterpiece
